title: Inspect the retry cost
lesson: Inspect nested spans to distinguish overall task time, a long billing operation, and the failed attempt and retry inside it.
transcript: 0–5.5s: A total duration of 2,400 ms leaves the slow operation unexplained.
5.5–13.5s: Inspection of a recorded trace progressively reveals the task span, a 200 ms retrieval, and a 2,000 ms billing operation.
13.5–18.4s: The billing operation contains a failed 1,200 ms first attempt, a 200 ms gap, and a successful 600 ms second attempt. The travelling chip says attempt 2: this is the first retry.

18.4–23s: The complete timeline holds, then the billing operation is selected for investigation. Its duration includes the failed attempt and the gap; it does not by itself prove why the remote service was slow.
23–26s: The scene fades to the matching black opening frame. Durations and identifiers are illustrative; the reveal is not retroactive instrumentation.

corrections.change: Changed retry 2 to attempt 2 so the packet agrees with the second-attempt row; preserved original timings and retry mechanism.

limitations: Illustrative synchronous waterfall; animation progressively reveals recorded spans rather than implementing tracing retroactively.
No concrete span IDs, parent-ID fields, propagation repair, sampling or export pipeline are shown. Nested durations must not be added to the parent duration.
The 200 ms gap is scripted backoff; the trace alone would not establish its cause.
Audio analysed only; no listening or device audibility check. Original model provenance was not recorded.
